description: This source file 'send-pack.c' implements the core functionality for the 'git send-pack' command in Git. It handles packaging objects, negotiating configurations with the remote, sending references, signing push certificates, managing sideband communication, and processing server responses during a push operation.

classes.name: struct send_pack_args
classes.description: Structure holding arguments and options for the send_pack operation, including flags, URLs, push options, and configuration settings.

classes.name: struct ref
classes.description: Represents a remote repository reference, containing its name, object IDs, status, and other push-related metadata.

classes.name: struct repository
classes.description: Represents the local repository context, containing configuration, the object database, and other repository-specific data.

classes.name: struct child_process
classes.description: Encapsulates context for spawning and managing subprocesses, including command arguments and I/O file descriptors.

methods.name: send_pack()
methods.description: Main function that coordinates the process of sending pack data and references to the remote, handling negotiation, signing, and response processing.

methods.name: pack_objects()
methods.description: Creates and streams the pack file containing objects that need to be transferred during the push.

methods.name: receive_status()
methods.description: Processes the server's response after sending data, updating reference statuses based on remote feedback.

methods.name: generate_push_cert()
methods.description: Creates and signs a push certificate detailing the refs being pushed, their old and new OIDs for authentication and verification.

methods.name: reject_invalid_nonce()
methods.description: Validates the push certificate nonce to ensure it contains only allowed characters, rejecting invalid nonces.

methods.name: get_commons_through_negotiation()
methods.description: Performs negotiation with the remote to identify common objects for efficient push, adjusting what needs to be sent.
